C1.name: FRC.Interactions.tetrahedral_group
C1.doc: 27:C1, 27:C4 — `SU(2, 𝔽₃)` over `𝔽₉`: `24 = q(q² − 1)` elements, closed under the product, non-abelian, every trace `a + ā` in the shell, the orders `1, 2, 3, 4, 6` in multiplicities `1, 1, 8, 6, 8` (the binary tetrahedral group), the traces `0, 1, 2` in multiplicities `6, 9, 9`; the drive `diag(i, −i) = (i, 0)` lies in the group and its centraliser has `4` elements.

C1.name: FRC.Unitary.class_function
C1.doc: 27:C1, 27:C4 — the trace is a class function: `Tr (g M g⁻¹) = Tr M` for `g` of determinant one, `g⁻¹` the adjugate; in general `Tr (g M adj g) = det g · Tr M`. The Wilson trace of a plaquette is gauge-invariant.

C2.name: FRC.Interactions.gauge_flux_invariant
C2.doc: 27:C2, 27:X1 — gauge invariance of the plaquette flux: with the corner gauges `φ₀, φ₁, φ₂, φ₃` and the links `A: 0 → 1`, `B: 1 → 2`, `C: 3 → 2`, `D: 0 → 3`, the transformed links `A + φ₁ − φ₀`, `B + φ₂ − φ₁`, `C + φ₂ − φ₃`, `D + φ₃ − φ₀` carry the flux `A + B − C − D` of the original.

C2.name: FRC.Interactions.projector_forced
C2.doc: 27:C2, 27:X3 — the photon's operator forced. A rotation-invariant quadratic symbol with constant part is `σ(k) = a k k + b |k|² δ + c δ`; gauge invariance, `σ(k) k = 0` for every `k`, reads `((a + b) |k|² + c) k = 0`, and its two evaluations at `|k|² = 1` and `|k|² = 2` give `a + b = 0` and `c = 0`: the symbol is `b (|k|² δ − k k)`, the transverse projector, massless (`c = 0`) and unique up to the one coefficient.

C2.name: FRC.Interactions.admissible_two
C2.doc: 27:C2, 27:X3 — the two admissible vectors satisfy every one of the `1 023` constraint rows (python's `13 338` rows distinct up to a scalar; that the range-1 translation-, gauge- and hypercubic-invariant quadratic actions at `L = 4` form exactly a two-dimensional space is the rank `121` of the rows, python's check A5), Maxwell's plaquette action satisfies them too, and it is their difference: `2 · Maxwell = B − A`.

C3.name: FRC.Interactions.green_torus
C3.doc: 27:C3 — the `L = 4` Coulomb Green's function in exact rationals: `7680 G` is the integer table, `ΔG = δ − 1/64` at every site (`7680 Δg = 7680 δ − 120`), `G(1, 0, 0) = 257/7680` (two unit charges at separation `1`), the table is cubic-symmetric on the axis and monotone `G(0) > G(1) > G(2)`, and its total is `0` (the zero mode removed).

C4.name: FRC.Interactions.drive_adjoint
C4.doc: 27:C4, 27:X1 — the drive on every shell. For the drive `δ = diag(g, h)` on a prime shell, with `g h = 1` and `g² ≠ 1`: `δ` fixes `H` and scales `E` and `F` by `g²` and `h²` (`adjoint_weights`); a matrix commutes with `δ` exactly when it is diagonal (`drive_commutes`); a matrix of determinant one commutes with `δ` exactly when it is `diag(a, d)` with `a d = 1`; each nonzero residue `a` gives one such matrix, `diag(a, a^(p−2))`, and `d` is decided by `a`; the nonzero residues are those of `1, …, p − 1` (`nonzero_residues`), so these matrices are the split cycle of order `p − 1`; and an element `[[a, ν b], [b, a]]` of the boost cycle with `b ≠ 0` does not commute with the drive.

C4.name: FRC.Unitary.drive_lift
C4.doc: 27:C15, 27:C4 — the entries `η = pt ν 0 1` and `η⁻¹ = pt ν 0 k`, `ν k = 1`, of the lift `diag(η, η⁻¹)` of one chronon. They are inverse, their squares are `ν` and `k`, the entries of the transport of two chronons, and their norms are `−ν` and `−k`. So one chronon multiplies the two charged directions by `η · η = ν` and `η⁻¹ · η⁻¹ = k`, and the Hermitian pairings of the two components by `−ν` and `−k`.

C4.name: FRC.Interactions.va_cancel
C4.doc: 27:C4, 27:X6 — the cancellation of a boost over its cycle: on a prime shell, for `u^N = 1` and `u^{2δ} ≠ 1`, `Σ_{τ<N} u^{2δτ} = 0` (the turning branch) while `Σ_{τ<N} 1 = N` (the constant branch).

C4.name: FRC.Interactions.orientation_flip
C4.doc: 27:C4, 27:X6 — the orientation convention `ε ↦ −ε` relabels the branches: the inverse exponent `2(N − δ)` is as far from the identity as `2δ` (`u^{2δ} u^{2(N−δ)} = u^{2N} = 1`), so its branch sums to `0` too; the two conventions disagree on the label (`1 ≠ −1`), and `ε · ε > 0` for both signs.

C5.name: FRC.Chirality.mass_form
C5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X5 — the mass form of the doublet in the basis of the four generators. With `w² = ν`, the unit vacuum `(0, 1)` and `a = g / 2`, `a′ = g′ / 2`, the generators send the vacuum to `(a, 0)`, `(a w, 0)`, `(0, −a w)` and `(0, a′ w)`. Their Frobenius-Hermitian pairings lie on the shell: `a²` and `−ν a²` for the charged pair, whose mixed pairing cancels; `−ν a²`, `−ν a′²` and the mixed sum `2 ν a a′` for the neutral pair.

C5.name: FRC.Chirality.mass_spectrum
C5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X5 — the spectrum of the mass form against the invariant form `diag(1, −ν, −ν, −ν)`: the second charged generator has the value `a²` of the first; `(a′, a)` is the kernel of the neutral block (the photon); and `(a, −a′)` has the value `a² + a′²`.

C5.name: FRC.Chirality.mass_independent
C5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X5 — the two neutral eigenvectors `(a′, a)` and `(a, −a′)` are independent when `a² + a′² ≠ 0`: a combination `x (a′, a) + y (a, −a′) = 0` has `(a² + a′²) x = 0` and `(a² + a′²) y = 0`.

C5.name: FRC.Chirality.mass_block_square
C5.doc: 27:C5 — the neutral block `N = [[a², −a a′], [−a a′, a′²]]` has `N² = (a² + a′²) N`, entry by entry. Where `a² + a′² = 0` it squares to zero: the excluded case of the mass form.

C5.name: FRC.Chirality.invariant_form
C5.doc: 27:C5 — the invariant form `−2 tr(T²)` on the generators with `h = 1/2`: `4h² = 1` for the first, `−4 ν h² = −ν` for the three that carry `w`.

C5.name: FRC.Interactions.neutral_block
C5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X3, 27:X5 — the neutral mass block, cleared of `¼`: with `m₀₀ = g² v²`, `m₀₁ = −g g′ v²`, `m₁₁ = g′² v²`, `m₀₀ m₁₁ − m₀₁² = 0` (the massless photon); `(m₀₀, m₀₁) · (g′, g) = 0` and `(m₀₁, m₁₁) · (g′, g) = 0`; the block applied to `(g, −g′)` returns `(g² + g′²) v² · (g, −g′)`.

C5.name: FRC.Interactions.five_eighths
C5.doc: 27:C5 — `M_W²/M_Z² = cos²θ_W = 5/8`: `M_W² = g² v²/4` and `M_Z² = (g² + g′²) v²/4`, so the ratio is `g²/(g² + g′²)`; where `sin²θ_W = g′²/(g² + g′²) = 3/8`, that is `8 g′² = 3 (g² + g′²)`, the ratio reads `8 g² = 5 (g² + g′²)`, on every shell.

C6.name: FRC.Interactions.weinberg_angle
C6.doc: 27:C6, 27:X4 — the Weinberg angle from the charge spectrum of one generation: over the sixteen states of `gen16`, `Σ (6T₃)² = 72` and `Σ (6Q)² = 192`, so `Tr T₃² = 2`, `Tr Q² = 16/3` and `sin²θ_W = Tr T₃²/Tr Q² = 72/192 = 3/8` (`72 · 8 = 192 · 3`).

C6.doc: 00:G11, 27:C6, 27:C8, 27:X2, 27:X8, 27:P2, 27:P3, 27:P5, 27:P6, 27:P7 — one generation as the spinor `16` of the rank-five frame read `3 + 2`. The content by multiplet (colour indices, weak indices, `6Y`): `(0,0,0)`, `(2,0,−4)` ×3, `(1,1,1)` ×6, `(0,2,6)`, `(3,1,−3)` ×2, `(2,2,2)` ×3, that is `ν^c + u^c + Q + e^c + L + d^c`; the charges `6Q`; the anomaly sums `Σ Y = Σ Y³ = 0`, `SU(3)²Y = 0` (the colour triplets and antitriplets), `SU(2)²Y = 0` (the doublets); as many triplets as antitriplets; an even number of doublets (Witten); and the right-handed neutrino, the state `∅`, neutral and a singlet; the charges `6Q` of the list give the proton's `6Q(uud) = 4 + 4 − 2 = 6 = 6Q(e⁺)` (27:X2).

C7.name: FRC.Interactions.su3_centre
C7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7, 35:C1, 35:X2 — the scalar centre of `SU(3, 2)` over `𝔽₄`: the scalars `x I` with `x x̄ = 1` and `x³ = 1` are the three cube roots of unity `1, w, w²` (`ℤ₃`, colour triality), `0` is not one, and each commutes with `U₁` and `U₂`; that the centre is no larger is 27-fields' ledger check E1 (all `216²` products) and, in the kernel, the hadrons theme's `FRC.Hadrons.colour_group` (the commutant of `D₁` and `U₁` in the group built by frames is the three scalars).

C7.name: FRC.Interactions.gluon_commutator
C7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7, 27:X1 — the gluon self-coupling over `𝔽₄`: the two elements `U₁ = [[0,0,1],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]]` and `U₂ = [[0,0,1],[0,w,0],[w²,0,0]]` of `SU(3, 2)` (`U†U = I`, `det U = 1`) do not commute, their commutator plaquette `U₁U₂U₁⁻¹U₂⁻¹ = diag(w², 1, w) ≠ I`, while the abelian control `D₁ = diag(1, w, w²)`, `D₂ = diag(w, 1, w²)` returns `I`.

C7.name: FRC.Interactions.rank_tower
C7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7 — the rank tower: for `Ω ≡ 5 (mod 12)` the cycle `Ω + 1 ≡ 6 (mod 12)` carries the ranks `1, 2, 3`, `2 ∣ Ω + 1` and `3 ∣ Ω + 1`, and stops there: `Ω + 1 ≡ 2 (mod 4)`, so `4 ∤ Ω + 1` and `gcd(4, Ω + 1) = 2`. The colour rank is `3`, the isospin rank `2`.

C8.name: FRC.Interactions.one_generation
C8.doc: 00:G11, 27:C6, 27:C8, 27:X2, 27:X8, 27:P2, 27:P3, 27:P5, 27:P6, 27:P7 — one generation as the spinor `16` of the rank-five frame read `3 + 2`. The content by multiplet (colour indices, weak indices, `6Y`): `(0,0,0)`, `(2,0,−4)` ×3, `(1,1,1)` ×6, `(0,2,6)`, `(3,1,−3)` ×2, `(2,2,2)` ×3, that is `ν^c + u^c + Q + e^c + L + d^c`; the charges `6Q`; the anomaly sums `Σ Y = Σ Y³ = 0`, `SU(3)²Y = 0` (the colour triplets and antitriplets), `SU(2)²Y = 0` (the doublets); as many triplets as antitriplets; an even number of doublets (Witten); and the right-handed neutrino, the state `∅`, neutral and a singlet; the charges `6Q` of the list give the proton's `6Q(uud) = 4 + 4 − 2 = 6 = 6Q(e⁺)` (27:X2).

C9.name: FRC.Interactions.unification_counts
C9.doc: 27:C9, 27:P4 — the unification counts: `dim SU(5) − dim (SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)) = 24 − (8 + 3 + 1) = 12 = 2 · (3 · 2)`, the colour–isospin off-block, the twelve `X, Y` leptoquarks; the spinor `16 = 1 + 5 + 10`; `dim SO(10) = 10 · 9 / 2 = 45`.

C9.name: FRC.Interactions.fifth_direction
C9.doc: 00:G12, 27:C9, 28:C12 — the quarter-turn as the fifth direction maps the sixteen `e_S` of four directions one-to-one onto the sixteen even subsets of five directions, the chiral spinor `16`; for `|S|` odd the image is the product `e_S e_4` with sign `+1`.

C9.name: FRC.Interactions.offblock_automorphism
C9.doc: 27:C9, 27:X8, 00:Z5 — each colour–isospin transposition is an automorphism of the reflection algebra of five directions up to the sign of the basis element: for all `S, T < 32`, `e_{τS} e_{τT}` vanishes exactly when `e_S e_T` does, and otherwise is `± e_{τ(S∪T)}`; the relabelling is a bijection of the `32` subsets.

C10.name: FRC.Ladder.tower_reduces
C10.doc: 26:G2, 27:C10, 27:X9, 27:P1, 28:X3, 00:G15 — a tower exponent is read modulo `n`: `g^{(g^j)} = g^{(g^j) mod n}`; tetration is exponentiation of a reduced index, and the two cyclic structures host every iterate (the ladder of the four roles closes: the fifth step returns to counting, 27-fields' C10).

C11.name: FRC.Interactions.residue_five
C11.doc: 27:C11 — `Ω ≡ 5 (mod 12)` is the conjunction `Ω ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `Ω ≡ 2 (mod 3)`, for every natural number: the twelve residues decide it, and the three moduli are periodic in `12`.

C11.name: FRC.Interactions.residue_instances
C11.doc: 27:C11 — the instances: the first eight admissible shells `5, 17, 29, 41, 53, 89, 101, 113` and the laboratory Carrier `Ω = 2 408 561` (37-sim) read `5 (mod 12)`; the Koide carriers `13, 61, 157, 421` read `1 (mod 12)` and fail the criterion.

C13.name: FRC.Chirality.chirality_square
C13.doc: 27:C13 — the square of the product of four pairwise anticommuting elements is the product of their squares, with no sign left over.

C13.name: FRC.Chirality.chirality_clifford
C13.doc: 27:C13 — with the Clifford relations of `diag(−c, 1, 1, 1)`, the product `Γ = γ⁰γ¹γ²γ³` has `Γ² ≈ −c`.

C13.name: FRC.Chirality.chirality_root
C13.doc: 27:C13 — for a central `u` with `u² ≈ −1` and `Γ² ≈ −c`, the element `uΓ` is a square root of `c`.

C13.name: FRC.Chirality.neg_nonsquare
C13.doc: 27:C13, 27:X6 — on a shell with `i² = −1`, if `ν` is a nonsquare then `−ν` is a nonsquare: `x² + ν` has no root, so an element with square `−ν` has no eigenvalue on the shell.

C13.name: FRC.Chirality.no_idempotent
C13.doc: 27:C13, 27:X6 — `𝔽_p[Γ]` holds no idempotent `a + bΓ` with `b` invertible: on a shell where `ν` is no square, `(a + bΓ)² = a + bΓ` and `b c = 1` are contradictory. An idempotent therefore has `b = 0` and is an idempotent of the shell.

C13.name: FRC.Chirality.root_sq
C13.doc: 27:C13 — `(i w)² = −ν` in the extension: `i w` and `−i w` are the roots of `x² + ν`.

C13.name: FRC.Chirality.root_conj
C13.doc: 27:C13, 27:X6 — the Frobenius conjugation exchanges the two roots `i w` and `−i w`.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.conj_shell
C14.doc: 27:C14 — the Frobenius conjugation fixes the shell's part of the extension.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.conj_root
C14.doc: 27:C13, 27:C14 — the Frobenius conjugation negates a multiple of `w`: it exchanges `i w` and `−i w`.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.shell_mul_shell
C14.doc: 27:C14 — the grading is multiplicative: shell times shell is on the shell.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.root_mul_shell
C14.doc: 27:C14 — a multiple of `w` times a shell element is a multiple of `w`.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.shell_mul_root
C14.doc: 27:C14 — a shell element times a multiple of `w` is a multiple of `w`.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.root_mul_root
C14.doc: 27:C14 — two multiples of `w` multiply to a shell element.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.drive_lift_frobenius
C14.doc: 27:C14 — an entry of the drive's lift times a shell element is negated by the Frobenius conjugation: on the coset of the lift, `σ(A) = −A` entry by entry.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.drive_lift_square
C14.doc: 27:C14 — the square of the lift's entry `w` is the shell element `ν`: the lift's square is over the shell.

C14.name: FRC.Chirality.tally_sign
C14.doc: 27:C14 — the sign cancels in a sesquilinear tally: `σ(−x)(−y) = σ(x) y`.

C15.name: FRC.Unitary.torus_cycles
C15.doc: 27:C15 — the diagonal torus over the extension and its two cycles: `diag_commutes`, `torus_weights`, `unitary_point`, `cycles_meet` and `drive_rescales` together.

C15.name: FRC.Unitary.cycle_orders
C15.doc: 27:C15 — the orders of the two cycles of the diagonal torus, on a prime shell with `ν` a nonsquare and `2 ≠ 0`. The split cycle: the nonzero residues are those of `1, …, p − 1`, each has `a^(p−1) = 1`, no `0 < m < p − 1` is a period of all of them, and one of them has order `p − 1`. The unitary cycle: its points are `−1` and the Cayley points of the `p` residues, pairwise distinct, each has `w^(p+1) = 1`, no `0 < d < p + 1` is a period of all of them, and one of them has order `p + 1`.

C15.name: FRC.Unitary.unit_cycle
C15.doc: 27:C15 — the units of the extension: the square of a unit with the kernel of the quotient `x/σ(x)`, the unitary points as such quotients, the two readings of a weight, and the split cycle of the unitary frame as rotations with entries of the shell.

C15.name: FRC.Unitary.drive_lift
C15.doc: 27:C15, 27:C4 — the entries `η = pt ν 0 1` and `η⁻¹ = pt ν 0 k`, `ν k = 1`, of the lift `diag(η, η⁻¹)` of one chronon. They are inverse, their squares are `ν` and `k`, the entries of the transport of two chronons, and their norms are `−ν` and `−k`. So one chronon multiplies the two charged directions by `η · η = ν` and `η⁻¹ · η⁻¹ = k`, and the Hermitian pairings of the two components by `−ν` and `−k`.

C15.name: FRC.Unitary.fixed_rays
C15.doc: 27:C15 — the rays that one chronon keeps. If `diag(g, 1)` multiplies the vector `(x, y)` by a scalar `c`, with `g − 1` invertible, then `x y = 0`: the ray is the origin or the antipode.

C16.name: FRC.Unitary.one_charge_system
C16.doc: 27:C16 — one charge system in the frame of rank five: the hypercharge cycle and the charge cycle have determinant one, the first is faithful, the second is trivial on the doublet exactly at the cube roots of unity, the weights on the sixteen states are `6Y` and `−3Q`, for `d ∣ p + 1`, `d > 1`, some unitary point is no `d`-th power, and where `p + 2 = 3 j` every unitary point is a cube.

C16.name: FRC.Unitary.power_classes
C16.doc: 27:C16 — the classes of the unitary cycle modulo its `d`-th powers, for `p + 1 = d m` and a generator `u`: every unitary point is `v^d · u^r` with `v` unitary and `r < d`, and `u^s` is no `d`-th power of a unitary point for `0 < s < d`. So the classes are those of `u^0, …, u^(d−1)`, and they number `d`.

C16.name: FRC.Unitary.sixth_powers
C16.doc: 27:C16 — the sixth powers of the unitary cycle are its `d`-th powers for `d = gcd(6, p + 1)`. The numbers `6 = d a`, `p + 1 = d m` and `a x = 1 + m t` certify the greatest common divisor: `d` divides both, and `a` is prime to `m`. Then `w⁶ = (w^a)^d`, and `v^d = (v^x)⁶` for a unitary `v`.

C16.name: FRC.Unitary.det_scale
C16.doc: 27:C16 — a scalar `s` multiplies the determinant of rank three by `s³` and that of rank two by `s²`. With `s = σ(w)²` on the colour block and `s = w³` on the doublet, the product of a hypercharge point with a pair of determinants one has the determinant `w⁶` on the doublet.

C16.name: FRC.Unitary.charge_squares
C16.doc: 27:C16 — a point of the charge cycle that is a product of a hypercharge point with a pair of determinants one is a square, and every square is such a product. The point `diag(u, u, u, σ(u)³, 1)` has the determinant `σ(u)³` on the doublet and the product has `w⁶`: from `σ(u)³ = w⁶` the unitary `z = (u w²)² w^p` has `z² = u`. Conversely, for a unitary `z` and `w = σ(z)`, `σ(z²)³ = w⁶`, and the block `diag(w³, z³)` has determinant one.

C16.name: FRC.Unitary.commutant_scalar
C16.doc: 27:C16 — a matrix of rank three over the extension that commutes with a diagonal matrix whose three entries have invertible differences, and with the two permutation matrices of adjacent directions, is a scalar. The three are unitary when the entries are unitary points, so a frame move of the colour block that commutes with every frame move of the block is a scalar: the centre of the vacuum's stabiliser is the charge cycle.

C16.name: FRC.Unitary.product_kernel
C16.doc: 27:C16, 27:P10 — the kernel of the product of the hypercharge cycle with the two frames of determinant one. A hypercharge point of a unitary `w` is `σ(w)² I₃` on the colour block and `w³ I₂` on the doublet. Its product with a pair `(A, B)` is the identity only for `A = w² I₃`, of determinant `w⁶`, and for `B = σ(w)³ I₂`, since `w³ σ(w)³ = 1`. The two determinants are one together, `w⁶ = 1` exactly when `σ(w)⁶ = 1`. So the kernel is the set of the triples with `w⁶ = 1`.

C16.name: FRC.Unitary.sixth_roots
C16.doc: 27:C16, 27:P10 — the solutions of `w⁶ = 1` on the unitary cycle, the kernel of the product map. With `6 = d a`, `p + 1 = d m`, `a x = 1 + m t` and a generator `u`: a unitary point has `w⁶ = 1` exactly when `w^d = 1`, and the unitary points with `w^d = 1` are the `d` distinct powers `u^(m r)`, `r < d`. The kernel is a cycle of order `d = gcd(6, p + 1)`.

C17.name: FRC.Unitary.tally_even
C17.doc: 27:C17 — an expression formed from the entries with integer coefficients commutes with the Frobenius: its value on the conjugate entries is the conjugate of its value. A value of the shell is its own conjugate, so a tally takes equal values on a configuration and on its Frobenius conjugate.

C17.name: FRC.Unitary.orientation_odd
C17.doc: 27:C17 — the orientation-odd term of a plaquette. For a frame move `U` of determinant one the difference of the traces of `U` and of its inverse is negated by the Frobenius, and its real part is `2`-torsion.

C17.name: FRC.Unitary.antihermitian_det
C17.doc: 27:C17 — the determinant of an anti-Hermitian matrix of three rows, such as the commutator of two Hermitian matrices, is negated by the Frobenius, and its real part is `2`-torsion.

C17.name: FRC.Unitary.odd_product
C17.doc: 27:C17 — the product of two elements that the Frobenius negates is fixed by it, and its imaginary part is `2`-torsion: on an odd shell the product lies in the shell.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.gauge_flux_invariant
X1.doc: 27:C2, 27:X1 — gauge invariance of the plaquette flux: with the corner gauges `φ₀, φ₁, φ₂, φ₃` and the links `A: 0 → 1`, `B: 1 → 2`, `C: 3 → 2`, `D: 0 → 3`, the transformed links `A + φ₁ − φ₀`, `B + φ₂ − φ₁`, `C + φ₂ − φ₃`, `D + φ₃ − φ₀` carry the flux `A + B − C − D` of the original.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.drive_adjoint
X1.doc: 27:C4, 27:X1 — the drive on every shell. For the drive `δ = diag(g, h)` on a prime shell, with `g h = 1` and `g² ≠ 1`: `δ` fixes `H` and scales `E` and `F` by `g²` and `h²` (`adjoint_weights`); a matrix commutes with `δ` exactly when it is diagonal (`drive_commutes`); a matrix of determinant one commutes with `δ` exactly when it is `diag(a, d)` with `a d = 1`; each nonzero residue `a` gives one such matrix, `diag(a, a^(p−2))`, and `d` is decided by `a`; the nonzero residues are those of `1, …, p − 1` (`nonzero_residues`), so these matrices are the split cycle of order `p − 1`; and an element `[[a, ν b], [b, a]]` of the boost cycle with `b ≠ 0` does not commute with the drive.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.gluon_commutator
X1.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7, 27:X1 — the gluon self-coupling over `𝔽₄`: the two elements `U₁ = [[0,0,1],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]]` and `U₂ = [[0,0,1],[0,w,0],[w²,0,0]]` of `SU(3, 2)` (`U†U = I`, `det U = 1`) do not commute, their commutator plaquette `U₁U₂U₁⁻¹U₂⁻¹ = diag(w², 1, w) ≠ I`, while the abelian control `D₁ = diag(1, w, w²)`, `D₂ = diag(w, 1, w²)` returns `I`.

X2.name: FRC.Interactions.holonomy_stokes
X2.doc: 27:X2, 27:C2 — discrete Stokes on a `2 × 1` rectangle: the holonomy of the boundary loop, `A₁ + A₂ + B₃ − A₄ − A₅ − B₀` (two bottom links, the right link, two top links, the left link), equals the sum of the two enclosed plaquette fluxes `F₁ = A₁ + B₁ − A₅ − B₀` and `F₂ = A₂ + B₃ − A₄ − B₁`, the shared link `B₁` cancelling; the holonomy is additive over adjacent loops.

X2.name: FRC.Interactions.one_generation
X2.doc: 00:G11, 27:C6, 27:C8, 27:X2, 27:X8, 27:P2, 27:P3, 27:P5, 27:P6, 27:P7 — one generation as the spinor `16` of the rank-five frame read `3 + 2`. The content by multiplet (colour indices, weak indices, `6Y`): `(0,0,0)`, `(2,0,−4)` ×3, `(1,1,1)` ×6, `(0,2,6)`, `(3,1,−3)` ×2, `(2,2,2)` ×3, that is `ν^c + u^c + Q + e^c + L + d^c`; the charges `6Q`; the anomaly sums `Σ Y = Σ Y³ = 0`, `SU(3)²Y = 0` (the colour triplets and antitriplets), `SU(2)²Y = 0` (the doublets); as many triplets as antitriplets; an even number of doublets (Witten); and the right-handed neutrino, the state `∅`, neutral and a singlet; the charges `6Q` of the list give the proton's `6Q(uud) = 4 + 4 − 2 = 6 = 6Q(e⁺)` (27:X2).

X3.name: FRC.Interactions.neutral_block
X3.doc: 27:C5, 27:X3, 27:X5 — the neutral mass block, cleared of `¼`: with `m₀₀ = g² v²`, `m₀₁ = −g g′ v²`, `m₁₁ = g′² v²`, `m₀₀ m₁₁ − m₀₁² = 0` (the massless photon); `(m₀₀, m₀₁) · (g′, g) = 0` and `(m₀₁, m₁₁) · (g′, g) = 0`; the block applied to `(g, −g′)` returns `(g² + g′²) v² · (g, −g′)`.

X3.name: FRC.Interactions.projector_forced
X3.doc: 27:C2, 27:X3 — the photon's operator forced. A rotation-invariant quadratic symbol with constant part is `σ(k) = a k k + b |k|² δ + c δ`; gauge invariance, `σ(k) k = 0` for every `k`, reads `((a + b) |k|² + c) k = 0`, and its two evaluations at `|k|² = 1` and `|k|² = 2` give `a + b = 0` and `c = 0`: the symbol is `b (|k|² δ − k k)`, the transverse projector, massless (`c = 0`) and unique up to the one coefficient.

X3.name: FRC.Interactions.admissible_two
X3.doc: 27:C2, 27:X3 — the two admissible vectors satisfy every one of the `1 023` constraint rows (python's `13 338` rows distinct up to a scalar; that the range-1 translation-, gauge- and hypercubic-invariant quadratic actions at `L = 4` form exactly a two-dimensional space is the rank `121` of the rows, python's check A5), Maxwell's plaquette action satisfies them too, and it is their difference: `2 · Maxwell = B − A`.

X4.name: FRC.Interactions.weinberg_angle
X4.doc: 27:C6, 27:X4 — the Weinberg angle from the charge spectrum of one generation: over the sixteen states of `gen16`, `Σ (6T₃)² = 72` and `Σ (6Q)² = 192`, so `Tr T₃² = 2`, `Tr Q² = 16/3` and `sin²θ_W = Tr T₃²/Tr Q² = 72/192 = 3/8` (`72 · 8 = 192 · 3`).

X5.name: FRC.Interactions.neutral_block
X5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X3, 27:X5 — the neutral mass block, cleared of `¼`: with `m₀₀ = g² v²`, `m₀₁ = −g g′ v²`, `m₁₁ = g′² v²`, `m₀₀ m₁₁ − m₀₁² = 0` (the massless photon); `(m₀₀, m₀₁) · (g′, g) = 0` and `(m₀₁, m₁₁) · (g′, g) = 0`; the block applied to `(g, −g′)` returns `(g² + g′²) v² · (g, −g′)`.

X5.name: FRC.Chirality.mass_form
X5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X5 — the mass form of the doublet in the basis of the four generators. With `w² = ν`, the unit vacuum `(0, 1)` and `a = g / 2`, `a′ = g′ / 2`, the generators send the vacuum to `(a, 0)`, `(a w, 0)`, `(0, −a w)` and `(0, a′ w)`. Their Frobenius-Hermitian pairings lie on the shell: `a²` and `−ν a²` for the charged pair, whose mixed pairing cancels; `−ν a²`, `−ν a′²` and the mixed sum `2 ν a a′` for the neutral pair.

X5.name: FRC.Chirality.mass_spectrum
X5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X5 — the spectrum of the mass form against the invariant form `diag(1, −ν, −ν, −ν)`: the second charged generator has the value `a²` of the first; `(a′, a)` is the kernel of the neutral block (the photon); and `(a, −a′)` has the value `a² + a′²`.

X5.name: FRC.Chirality.mass_independent
X5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X5 — the two neutral eigenvectors `(a′, a)` and `(a, −a′)` are independent when `a² + a′² ≠ 0`: a combination `x (a′, a) + y (a, −a′) = 0` has `(a² + a′²) x = 0` and `(a² + a′²) y = 0`.

X6.name: FRC.Chirality.neg_nonsquare
X6.doc: 27:C13, 27:X6 — on a shell with `i² = −1`, if `ν` is a nonsquare then `−ν` is a nonsquare: `x² + ν` has no root, so an element with square `−ν` has no eigenvalue on the shell.

X6.name: FRC.Chirality.no_idempotent
X6.doc: 27:C13, 27:X6 — `𝔽_p[Γ]` holds no idempotent `a + bΓ` with `b` invertible: on a shell where `ν` is no square, `(a + bΓ)² = a + bΓ` and `b c = 1` are contradictory. An idempotent therefore has `b = 0` and is an idempotent of the shell.

X6.name: FRC.Chirality.root_conj
X6.doc: 27:C13, 27:X6 — the Frobenius conjugation exchanges the two roots `i w` and `−i w`.

X6.name: FRC.Interactions.orientation_flip
X6.doc: 27:C4, 27:X6 — the orientation convention `ε ↦ −ε` relabels the branches: the inverse exponent `2(N − δ)` is as far from the identity as `2δ` (`u^{2δ} u^{2(N−δ)} = u^{2N} = 1`), so its branch sums to `0` too; the two conventions disagree on the label (`1 ≠ −1`), and `ε · ε > 0` for both signs.

X7.name: FRC.Interactions.su3_centre
X7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7, 35:C1, 35:X2 — the scalar centre of `SU(3, 2)` over `𝔽₄`: the scalars `x I` with `x x̄ = 1` and `x³ = 1` are the three cube roots of unity `1, w, w²` (`ℤ₃`, colour triality), `0` is not one, and each commutes with `U₁` and `U₂`; that the centre is no larger is 27-fields' ledger check E1 (all `216²` products) and, in the kernel, the hadrons theme's `FRC.Hadrons.colour_group` (the commutant of `D₁` and `U₁` in the group built by frames is the three scalars).

X7.name: FRC.Interactions.gluon_commutator
X7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7, 27:X1 — the gluon self-coupling over `𝔽₄`: the two elements `U₁ = [[0,0,1],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]]` and `U₂ = [[0,0,1],[0,w,0],[w²,0,0]]` of `SU(3, 2)` (`U†U = I`, `det U = 1`) do not commute, their commutator plaquette `U₁U₂U₁⁻¹U₂⁻¹ = diag(w², 1, w) ≠ I`, while the abelian control `D₁ = diag(1, w, w²)`, `D₂ = diag(w, 1, w²)` returns `I`.

X7.name: FRC.Interactions.rank_tower
X7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7 — the rank tower: for `Ω ≡ 5 (mod 12)` the cycle `Ω + 1 ≡ 6 (mod 12)` carries the ranks `1, 2, 3`, `2 ∣ Ω + 1` and `3 ∣ Ω + 1`, and stops there: `Ω + 1 ≡ 2 (mod 4)`, so `4 ∤ Ω + 1` and `gcd(4, Ω + 1) = 2`. The colour rank is `3`, the isospin rank `2`.

X8.name: FRC.Interactions.one_generation
X8.doc: 00:G11, 27:C6, 27:C8, 27:X2, 27:X8, 27:P2, 27:P3, 27:P5, 27:P6, 27:P7 — one generation as the spinor `16` of the rank-five frame read `3 + 2`. The content by multiplet (colour indices, weak indices, `6Y`): `(0,0,0)`, `(2,0,−4)` ×3, `(1,1,1)` ×6, `(0,2,6)`, `(3,1,−3)` ×2, `(2,2,2)` ×3, that is `ν^c + u^c + Q + e^c + L + d^c`; the charges `6Q`; the anomaly sums `Σ Y = Σ Y³ = 0`, `SU(3)²Y = 0` (the colour triplets and antitriplets), `SU(2)²Y = 0` (the doublets); as many triplets as antitriplets; an even number of doublets (Witten); and the right-handed neutrino, the state `∅`, neutral and a singlet; the charges `6Q` of the list give the proton's `6Q(uud) = 4 + 4 − 2 = 6 = 6Q(e⁺)` (27:X2).

X8.name: FRC.Interactions.offblock_automorphism
X8.doc: 27:C9, 27:X8, 00:Z5 — each colour–isospin transposition is an automorphism of the reflection algebra of five directions up to the sign of the basis element: for all `S, T < 32`, `e_{τS} e_{τT}` vanishes exactly when `e_S e_T` does, and otherwise is `± e_{τ(S∪T)}`; the relabelling is a bijection of the `32` subsets.

X9.name: FRC.Ladder.tower_reduces
X9.doc: 26:G2, 27:C10, 27:X9, 27:P1, 28:X3, 00:G15 — a tower exponent is read modulo `n`: `g^{(g^j)} = g^{(g^j) mod n}`; tetration is exponentiation of a reduced index, and the two cyclic structures host every iterate (the ladder of the four roles closes: the fifth step returns to counting, 27-fields' C10).

X10.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_parseval
X10.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C1, 28:X1 — Parseval on the cube-root orbit `C₃`: for amplitudes `a₀, a₁, a₂` and `ω` with `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`, `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 â₁ â₂`, `â₀ = Σ a_j`, `â₁ = a₀ + a₁ω + a₂ω²`, `â₂ = a₀ + a₁ω² + a₂ω` — the Koide form `Q = Σ a_j² / (Σ a_j)² = 1/3 + (2/3)ρ²` with `ρ² = â₁â₂/â₀²`, exact on every shell carrying the root `ω`.

X10.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_extension
X10.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C2, 28:X1, 28:P1, on every shell: with `h + h = 1` and `ν = −3`, `ω = −h + h w` has `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`; `â₂ = â̄₁`, so `â₁ â₂ = N(â₁)`; Parseval `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 N(â₁)`; and `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 N(â₁) = â₀²` (`ρ² = 1/2`).

X10.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_half
X10.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:X1 — the hypotheses of `koide_extension` hold on every frame `p = 4κ + 1`, the Carrier included: `h = 2κ + 1` has `h + h = 1`, and `ν = −3` has `ν + 3 = 0`.

X11.name: FRC.Unitary.wilson_orientation_even
X11.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the Wilson plaquette term `tr U + conj (tr U)`, twice the real part of the trace, is unchanged when the plaquette's orientation is reversed, `U ↦ U⁻¹`: for `U ∈ SU(3)`, `U⁻¹ = U†` and `tr U† = conj (tr U)`. The term is orientation-even, so the Wilson action class (the realisation B2) carries no orientation-odd term, no topological term.

X11.name: FRC.Unitary.hermitian_det_real
X11.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the determinant of a Hermitian `3 × 3` matrix over the extension is its own conjugate: `A† = A` gives `conj (det A) = det A`; its imaginary part is then `2`-torsion (`hermitian_det_shell`), so on every odd shell `det A` lies in the shell and `arg det A = 0`.

X11.name: FRC.Unitary.gram_det
X11.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the square of a Hermitian matrix: `det (A A) = det A · det A`, with `det A` its own conjugate and its imaginary part `2`-torsion. Where `det A` lies in the shell, `det (A A)` is the square of a residue of the shell.

X11.name: FRC.Unitary.hermitian_det_shell
X11.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the determinant of a Hermitian `3 × 3` matrix has `2`-torsion imaginary part: on every odd shell it lies in the shell.

X11.name: FRC.Interactions.ckm_free
X11.doc: 27:X11 — over `𝔽₁₇[√−3]` and `𝔽₅₃[√−3]`: the textured up and down mass matrices and the circulant are Hermitian (`M† = M` entrywise), their determinants are nonzero and lie in the shell with `det (M_u M_d)` (`arg det = 0`, the strong-CP angle vanishes), and `[M_u, M_d] ≠ 0` (no flavour symmetry forces the two to be simultaneously diagonal).

P8.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_parseval
P8.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C1, 28:X1 — Parseval on the cube-root orbit `C₃`: for amplitudes `a₀, a₁, a₂` and `ω` with `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`, `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 â₁ â₂`, `â₀ = Σ a_j`, `â₁ = a₀ + a₁ω + a₂ω²`, `â₂ = a₀ + a₁ω² + a₂ω` — the Koide form `Q = Σ a_j² / (Σ a_j)² = 1/3 + (2/3)ρ²` with `ρ² = â₁â₂/â₀²`, exact on every shell carrying the root `ω`.

P8.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_extension
P8.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C2, 28:X1, 28:P1, on every shell: with `h + h = 1` and `ν = −3`, `ω = −h + h w` has `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`; `â₂ = â̄₁`, so `â₁ â₂ = N(â₁)`; Parseval `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 N(â₁)`; and `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 N(â₁) = â₀²` (`ρ² = 1/2`).

P8.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_half

P9.name: FRC.Unitary.wilson_orientation_even
P9.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the Wilson plaquette term `tr U + conj (tr U)`, twice the real part of the trace, is unchanged when the plaquette's orientation is reversed, `U ↦ U⁻¹`: for `U ∈ SU(3)`, `U⁻¹ = U†` and `tr U† = conj (tr U)`. The term is orientation-even, so the Wilson action class (the realisation B2) carries no orientation-odd term, no topological term.

P9.name: FRC.Unitary.hermitian_det_real
P9.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the determinant of a Hermitian `3 × 3` matrix over the extension is its own conjugate: `A† = A` gives `conj (det A) = det A`; its imaginary part is then `2`-torsion (`hermitian_det_shell`), so on every odd shell `det A` lies in the shell and `arg det A = 0`.

P9.name: FRC.Unitary.gram_det
P9.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the square of a Hermitian matrix: `det (A A) = det A · det A`, with `det A` its own conjugate and its imaginary part `2`-torsion. Where `det A` lies in the shell, `det (A A)` is the square of a residue of the shell.

P9.name: FRC.Unitary.hermitian_det_shell
P9.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the determinant of a Hermitian `3 × 3` matrix has `2`-torsion imaginary part: on every odd shell it lies in the shell.

P10.name: FRC.Unitary.charge_weights
P10.doc: 27:C16, 27:P10 — on the sixteen states the weight of the hypercharge cycle, `−2 |S ∩ C| + 3 |S ∩ W|`, is `6Y`, and the weight of the charge cycle, `|S ∩ C| − 3 [3 ∈ S]`, is `−3Q`, so `6Q + 2 |S ∩ C|` is a multiple of `6`: a cube root of unity of the charge cycle acts as the centre of the colour frame. The first clause holds by the definition of `y6`, which `one_generation` ties to `6Y`.

P10.name: FRC.Unitary.product_kernel
P10.doc: 27:C16, 27:P10 — the kernel of the product of the hypercharge cycle with the two frames of determinant one. A hypercharge point of a unitary `w` is `σ(w)² I₃` on the colour block and `w³ I₂` on the doublet. Its product with a pair `(A, B)` is the identity only for `A = w² I₃`, of determinant `w⁶`, and for `B = σ(w)³ I₂`, since `w³ σ(w)³ = 1`. The two determinants are one together, `w⁶ = 1` exactly when `σ(w)⁶ = 1`. So the kernel is the set of the triples with `w⁶ = 1`.

P10.name: FRC.Unitary.sixth_roots
P10.doc: 27:C16, 27:P10 — the solutions of `w⁶ = 1` on the unitary cycle, the kernel of the product map. With `6 = d a`, `p + 1 = d m`, `a x = 1 + m t` and a generator `u`: a unitary point has `w⁶ = 1` exactly when `w^d = 1`, and the unitary points with `w^d = 1` are the `d` distinct powers `u^(m r)`, `r < d`. The kernel is a cycle of order `d = gcd(6, p + 1)`.

P10.name: FRC.Unitary.centre_weight
P10.doc: 27:P10 — the weight of a point of the centre of the colour frame. For a cube root of unity `x ≠ 1` the power `x ^ n` is one exactly when three divides `n`: a state of `n` net colour indices that the point fixes has `n` a multiple of three.

P10.name: FRC.Unitary.colourless_indices
P10.doc: 27:P10 — a state that the diagonal frame moves of the colour frame fix. With `aᵢ` indices and `bᵢ` conjugate indices in the colour direction `i`, fewer than `p + 1` in each sum, the equal weights `u^(a₁+b₃) = u^(a₃+b₁)` and `u^(a₂+b₃) = u^(a₃+b₂)` on a generator `u` of the unitary cycle give equal net numbers of indices in the three directions.
